sections.h2: Where do Henry County property tax bills come from?
sections.html:
Henry County runs its own billing through the Tax Commissioner, with a separate Board of Assessors deciding what each parcel is worth. The commissioner receives the money for the county, schools and other levying bodies and hands it on. Billing questions and value questions land at different desks, so choose before you dial.

Drop boxes sit at both commissioner offices. For mailed checks, make them payable to Henry County Tax Commissioner or HCTC, send them to 140 Henry Pkwy, and write the bill numbers on the check. The county refuses metered mail as evidence of timely mailing.

sections.h2: What is Henry County like, and what do its housing numbers show?
sections.html:
Georgia formed Henry County in 1821 from Creek lands, and its annual financial report places it about 25 miles southeast of downtown Atlanta. Its neighbors are DeKalb (north), Rockdale and Newton (east), Spalding and Butts (south) and Clayton (west). The county seat is McDonough, joined by the cities of Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove. The same report counts seven Interstate 75 interchanges inside the county and mentions a planned eighth at Bethlehem Road.

QuickFacts shows 264,922 residents in July 2025 across 318.71 square miles of land, about 755 people per square mile when the 2020 count was taken, many times Heard County's density. Permit offices issued 1,666 permits in 2025, so unsold new homes and resales share the market.

  • Typical owner-occupied home: $313,900 (2020 to 2024 median).
  • Homeowners hold 74.9% of occupied housing.
  • Rent at the median: $1,674 per month.
  • Median household income: $83,146.
  • Typical one-way commute: 33.1 minutes.

At those values, a small error in the square footage on file moves the bill, so check your digest record before setting a price.

sections.h2: What is the Henry County property tax deadline?
sections.html:
The commissioner's bill page says statements go to the January 1 owner and are payable on or before November 16, and the FAQ says mailing happens by mid-September. Counties may move the statewide December 20 default earlier, which is what this date reflects. For the 2022 digest, the fiscal 2023 financial report records a levy on August 11, billing on September 10 and a payment deadline of November 16. Whatever the calendar says, follow the date on the bill you receive.

Late payment gets costly. The commissioner says interest builds monthly and a further 5% penalty attaches every 120 days after the deadline, up to a ceiling of 20%. Mailed checks need a USPS postmark before the deadline. Since December 2025 the county reads that mark as the first automated processing date at a regional center, which can be later than the day you dropped the envelope off. A transfer from your bank's own bill-pay service has no postmark, so the money must be in hand by the deadline.

  • The online portal charges 2.5% on cards or $1.50 for an e-check, a fee set by its outside processor.
  • Daily ceilings are $20,000 on cards and $60,000 on e-checks.
  • Paying at a counter does not waive the card fee.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the lender is the contact for the bill.

sections.h2: Will Henry County bill the buyer after closing?
sections.html:
Not automatically. Statements go to the person who owned on January 1, and Henry's page explains the risk: a lien is filed against that owner unless the office receives a settlement statement inside 90 days of the due date, per Georgia Code 48-3-3. Send page one, where county taxes appear as collected, to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov with the address or a copy of the bill.

State revenue officials add that the owner on January 1 is responsible for the entire year with no partial refund. Look at the Henry County line on your closing statement before signing, and as the seller, send the paper yourself instead of assuming someone else did.

Other charges can share the bill. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation fees appear on it, and a county water charge called the 2 mill tax pays for storage and pipes whether or not a home has a well. The Water Authority at 770-957-6659 explains that line.

sections.h2: How does a Henry County homestead application work?
sections.html:
File in person at either commissioner office, through the online option, or by mail postmarked on or before April 1, since only a USPS postmark counts. One filing covers you for as long as you stay put. Bring these items.

  • Driver's licenses for you and your spouse that show the property address.
  • Registrations for every vehicle at that address.
  • The warranty deed.
  • A letter from any other county or state where you own a house, confirming no homestead is claimed there.
  • The divorce decree, if one applies.

Turning 62 by January 1 opens an added reduction on the school portion of assessed value, and approved exemptions step up again at ages 65, 68 and 70. The disability version asks for two doctors' letters, or one doctor's letter with a Social Security award letter, describing 100% disability. A married couple gets only one homestead.

sections.h2: What if I think my Henry County value is wrong?
sections.html:
Count 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Tax Assessor menu on the county site includes Notice of Assessment, Property Appeals, an appeal FAQ and conservation use rules, and the state's uniform PT-311A form asks you to commit to a route.

  • Board of Equalization: the route for value, uniformity, taxability or exemption fights. Henry lists this board under the Clerk of Superior Court, with its own members, forms, calendar, FAQ and appeal process pages.
  • Hearing officer: available only when non-homestead real estate exceeds $500,000.
  • Arbitration: restricted to value, and it needs a certified appraisal 45 days after the county acknowledges the appeal.

A superior court appeal follows written notice given within 30 days of the decision, after last year's tax is paid. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, as the state revenue department summarizes it, a final value of 85 percent or less of the board's figure entitles the owner to litigation costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

sections.h2: What happens if a Henry County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The commissioner runs judicial in rem tax sales at 140 Henry Parkway on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 AM. Once a sale happens, a twelve-month redemption period opens for interested parties, who repay the buyer's bid plus later taxes, assessments and a 20% premium, as Georgia's consumer office explains. Before a sale, paying the tax along with fees, penalties and interest releases the lien.

If you are selling with a lien open, ask the closing agent for a payoff figure well ahead of time. For background on the rate, the fiscal 2023 report lists the county general fund at 12.733 mills, level since fiscal 2017. Other levies are separate, so ask the commissioner what else appears on yours.

faqs.q: When are Henry County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The commissioner's page prints November 16, and bills mail by mid-September to the January 1 owner. The state default is December 20, so trust the date on your own bill.

faqs.q: How do I keep a Henry County lien off my name after selling?
faqs.a: Email page one of the settlement statement to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov inside the 90-day window. Without it the office records a lien against the January 1 owner.

faqs.q: How steep are Henry County late penalties?
faqs.a: Interest builds monthly, and 5% more is added every 120 days until penalties hit 20%. Make sure a mailed check has a USPS postmark before the deadline.

faqs.q: Where can I check a Henry County parcel's value?
faqs.a: Use the records search in the Tax Assessor section of the county website, or call (770) 288-7999, option 1. Billing questions go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 288-8180.

faqs.q: Can I appeal in Henry County while my house is listed?
faqs.a: Yes. Listing does not pause or cancel the 45-day window. A lower final value also shrinks the bill that is divided at closing.
